Seats held by the state's winning party.
floor(total_acs / 2) + 1. Constant per state per delimitation cycle.
Total nameplate generating capacity in megawatts, summed across all fuels, for India. Snapshot end-of-month from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary.
indicators.description_long: Nameplate capacity is the maximum sustained output a plant can deliver under ideal conditions — NOT the energy it actually produced. A state with high capacity isn't necessarily a high-generation state if those plants run at low plant-load factor (PLF). Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the five atomic-fuel children (coal + gas + hydro + nuclear + renewable). No `_total_mw` row exists on disk (ADR-0030 D33.8 refusal).
indicators.methodology_vintage: CEA Monthly Executive Summary — Installed Capacity (IC) sheet; snapshot reported month-end. Sub-fuel taxonomy stable through current vintage; coal+lignite combined per CEA convention.

indicators.description_short: Coal-fired thermal capacity. India's largest fuel category nationally (~42%).
Natural-gas and liquid-fuel thermal capacity. Stranded-fuel risk; small share.
Conventional (>25 MW) plus small-hydro capacity. Site-bound; multi-decade lifetime.
Nuclear capacity. Central-sector only; allocated to states via PPAs.

indicators.description_short: Wind, solar, biomass and waste-to-energy. Rapid growth; ~30% national capacity by FY26.

indicators.label_long: State installed electricity capacity, geographical-location basis (MW)
indicators.description_short: Total installed capacity physically located in the state, summed across all fuels. 'Geographical' means every plant counts toward the state where it sits, regardless of who owns it or where the power is dispatched.
indicators.description_long: Read this as 'where the steel-and-concrete sits' — NOT 'where the electricity flows to'. For the share-allocated counterpart (rights to output via central-sector PPAs), see state-installed-capacity-allocated-mw. The all-India total equals the allocated total (as it must) but the per-state breakdown diverges sharply for states that import or export power through central PPAs. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED capacity-metatable rollup of CEA-published station-level capacity; harmonised across fiscal years 2015-16 onwards.

indicators.label_long: State installed electricity capacity, allocated-shares basis (MW)
indicators.description_short: Same as the geographical-location capacity, but each state credited its share of joint-sector and central-sector plants per regional allocation formulas. Use this when comparing 'rights to electricity' rather than 'physical assets sited here'.
indicators.description_long: The all-India total equals the geographical total (as it must) but the per-state breakdown can diverge sharply: a state with little local capacity but large central-PPA shares has higher allocated capacity than geographical. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive API for FY15-FY25 (fiscal years 2015-16 onwards); RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 140 (silver tier; republishes CEA originals) for the pre-FY15 splice (fiscal years 2004-05 to 2013-14). Per plan-doc 20260522 §3 Q-c Option 1 SPLICE: methodology break at FY15 (basis change + RBI portion carries no per-fuel breakdown).

indicators.description_short: Total installed capacity allocated to each state at the end of the most recent month, from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary IC sheet. Snapshot view; complements the multi-FY ICED geographical and allocated series.
indicators.description_long: End-of-month, point-in-time snapshot from the CEA Monthly Executive Summary 'IC' sheet. Allocation basis (where the power is dispatched, including central-sector PPA shares) — different from the geographical-location series which counts plants by where they physically sit. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children. Single vintage per release; restate on each fresh CEA monthly drop rather than appending — citizen comparability is snapshot-only across states, NOT a time series.
indicators.methodology_vintage: CEA Monthly Executive Summary — IC sheet snapshot 2026-03

indicators.description_short: Per-state actual electricity generated, summed across all fuels. The delivered counterpart to installed capacity — capacity is potential, generation is what plants actually produced.
indicators.description_long: Most-recent fiscal year is partial-year-actuals + forecast and may revise; treat the most-recent two FYs as preliminary. Compute-on-read parent: sums the five atomic-fuel children. ICED's 'Others' bucket (interstate/central plants pre-allocation) is dropped because it cannot be mapped to a state choropleth honestly. 1 MU (million unit) = 1 GWh.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED /v1/gen-metatable-data (CEA-sourced upstream).

indicators.description_short: Coal-fired generation. ~70% of all-India electricity by GWh (PLF gap between capacity share and generation share).
Gas-fired generation. Capacity-rich, generation-poor due to fuel-supply constraints.
Hydroelectric generation. Seasonal (monsoon-dependent) and falling as a share over time.
Nuclear generation. Small share but rising as new units commission.
Wind, solar and biomass generation. ~10% all-India share by FY26; growing fast.

Total electricity actually billed to end-consumers (domestic + commercial + industrial + agricultural + public-lighting) in the state, in million units (MU). The gap between Generation and Sales is the absolute AT&C loss.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive; underlying figures from PFC State Distribution Utilities report. Includes intra-state imports — consumption can exceed in-state generation.

indicators.label_long: Aggregate Technical & Commercial losses (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Combined technical (transmission + distribution heat / ageing losses) and commercial (theft + uncollected billing) losses as % of energy input to the distribution system. Headline discom-health metric: lower is better.
indicators.description_long: Calculated by Power Finance Corporation from PFC State Distribution Utilities reports. UDAY (2015) targeted all-India AT&C below 15% by 2018-19; the actual all-India figure has hovered around 15% since then. State-level dispersion is wide — Gujarat / Andhra at ~6-10%, Bihar / J&K at ~25-40%.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive API row 'AT&C Losses'. Calculation method: PFC. Vintage updated annually with PFC report release (typically Q3 FY+1).

indicators.description_short: Highest single-instant electricity demand observed in the state during the fiscal year (MW). 'Peak' is system-wide simultaneous demand recorded by the State Load Despatch Centre — typically a summer afternoon (north / west) or winter evening (Punjab, Delhi).
indicators.description_long: Read alongside Peak Met (state-peak-electricity-supplied-mw) — the gap is the unmet peak demand, more operationally critical than the energy-deficit % because shortages force load-shedding. RBI Handbook relabelled 'Surplus / Deficit' to 'Demand Not Met' from FY 2019-20 onwards; underlying definition is unchanged.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 142. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Maximum instantaneous power actually supplied in the state during the fiscal year (MW). The pair (peak_demand, peak_supplied) tells the load-shedding story: supplied < demand in any year means the grid dropped load to keep frequency stable.
indicators.description_long: India's all-India peak deficit fell from ~12% in FY05 to under 1% from FY18 onwards, but state-level shortfalls persist — Bihar, UP, Punjab, J&K, and Andhra Pradesh routinely under-met their own peak in the FY13-FY25 window.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 142 (Peak Met column). Originating data: Central Electricity Authority.

indicators.description_short: Electricity consumption per person per year, in kilowatt-hours. Proxy for BOTH energy access (electrified homes) AND industrial intensity (heavy-industry load) — read alongside per-capita income to disambiguate.
indicators.description_long: A high value can mean many electrified domestic consumers (Kerala) OR a heavy-industry economy (Chhattisgarh, Odisha) OR both (Gujarat). A low value can mean a rural agrarian economy (Bihar, Assam) OR poor access (UP). The denominator (population) is Census 2011 + projection, so values for the 2020s are subject to mid-decade re-basing once Census 2027 data lands.
indicators.methodology_vintage: ICED composition: state electricity sales (CEA) divided by state population (Census 2011 + linear projection).

indicators.description_short: Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable sub-indicators of distribution-side efficiency — billing efficiency, collection efficiency, and T&D loss. The first two decompose the COMMERCIAL half of AT&C losses; the third is the TECHNICAL half.
indicators.description_long: Billing × Collection ÷ 100 = (1 − commercial-loss%); add the T&D loss% and you arrive at the AT&C loss% reported by state-atc-losses-pct. Per Hans D29 the parent row carries no source_id and no dimension_values; the three children inherit their source_id from ICED operational-performance and encode their facet via the efficiency_dimension axis.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED `/energy/electricity/distribution/operationalPerformanceStates`. Three categories: `billing-efficiency`, `collection-efficiency`, `td-loss`.

indicators.description_short: Share of energy actually billed to a consumer, out of total energy input to the distribution system. 100% = every kWh that enters the grid was billed.
indicators.description_long: The complement of billing-side losses (theft, unmetered consumption, under-billing). Together with collection efficiency, billing efficiency decomposes the commercial half of AT&C losses: AT&C loss ≈ 1 − (billing × collection / 100).

indicators.description_short: Share of billed revenue actually collected from consumers, by state. 100% = every rupee billed was paid.
indicators.description_long: Captures the second commercial dimension: how much of the energy that WAS billed got paid for. Together with billing efficiency, collection efficiency decomposes the commercial half of AT&C losses: AT&C loss ≈ 1 − (billing × collection / 100). Low collection often reflects high accounts-receivable days on government / agricultural / municipal consumer categories.

indicators.description_short: Transmission and Distribution loss as % of energy input — the TECHNICAL half of AT&C losses (heat / ageing / unmetered consumption on the wires).
indicators.description_long: T&D loss + commercial-loss = AT&C loss. Where AT&C is a comprehensive ledger of revenue leakage, T&D isolates the part attributable to physical infrastructure (line losses, transformer inefficiency). Older meters and longer rural feeders correlate with higher T&D loss; sub-station upgrades and HVDS rollout drive it down.

indicators.label_long: ACS-ARR gap on electricity sales (₹/kWh, by state)
indicators.description_short: Average Cost of Supply minus Average Revenue Realised, per unit of electricity sold. Positive = the utility loses money on every unit it sells (closed by tariff hike, loss reduction, or state subsidy). Zero is the UDAY/RDSS policy goal.
indicators.description_long: The structural per-unit loss of a discom: positive means it loses money on every kWh sold; negative means surplus. Calculated by PFC from utility tariff orders + audited accounts. Note the opposite sign convention from fiscal-deficit indicators — here a NEGATIVE number is the surplus side.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED state-wise deep-dive row 'ACS-ARR (Electricity Sales) Gap'. Calculated by PFC from utility tariff orders + audited accounts.

indicators.label_long: Renewable Purchase Obligation compliance (%, by state)
indicators.description_short: Compute-on-read parent: the three citizen-readable segments of state RPO compliance — solar, non-solar, and combined-target. Each measures share of the regulatory RPO target met, expressed as compliance ÷ target × 100.
indicators.description_long: Each state regulator sets a year-by-year RPO target as a % of total energy procurement; this parent groups the three segment-specific compliance ratios. The 'total' segment is NOT the sum of solar + non-solar — it is the combined-target compliance ratio (its own regulatory denominator). Values above 100% indicate over-compliance. Targets themselves vary by state and rise over time, so a 95% compliance in FY21 may represent more renewables than 105% in FY19.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED `/energy/electricity/distribution/rpo` (MNRE / state-regulator data). Three facets: `solar` (solarCompliance), `non-solar` (nonSolarCompliance), `total` (totalCompliance).

indicators.description_short: Share of the state's solar-specific RPO target actually met. 100% = solar-RPO target exactly met; values above 100% indicate over-compliance on solar procurement.
Share of the state's non-solar (wind + biomass + small-hydro) RPO target actually met. The 'other-renewables' segment of the obligation, regulated separately from the solar segment.
Combined-target RPO compliance — share of the state's overall (solar + non-solar combined) RPO target met. NOT the sum of solar + non-solar — the combined target is its own regulatory ratio.

Annual energy requirement assessed by the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year — the demand-side counterpart to availability. Requirement minus availability gives the 'energy not supplied' deficit.
indicators.description_long: The percentage gap (deficit / requirement) is the headline 'power deficit %' India tracked closely through the 2000s. The all-India deficit shrank from ~10% in FY05 to under 0.5% from FY18 onwards as supply caught up; persistent state-level deficits today flag distribution / scheduling issues, not generation shortage. Direction is neutral because higher requirement reflects both industrial activity (good) and inefficient consumption (not good) — interpret in conjunction with per-capita GSDP and T&D loss series.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 141. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Annual energy actually supplied to the state (MU = million units = GWh), fiscal year. The supply-side companion to Requirement (T141). Requirement − Availability = the energy-not-supplied deficit.
indicators.description_long: RBI Handbook Table 139 publishes the long-arc state-wise availability series sourced from CEA. Read alongside Requirement (T141): the percentage gap is the operational power-deficit metric. The all-India figure has converged on near-zero deficit since FY18, but state-level deficits persist for grid-island / load-shedding states.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 139. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.description_short: Annual per-capita electricity availability (kWh / person / year), by state and Union Territory, fiscal year. The most citizen-relevant single number for 'how much power do people in this state actually get to use' — captures both supply expansion and transmission losses.
indicators.description_long: Computed by CEA as state energy availability (MU) ÷ state mid-year population. The all-India figure roughly tripled from ~600 kWh in FY05 to ~1300 kWh in FY24, but the inter-state spread is wide (Goa / Punjab / Gujarat above 2,000; Bihar / Manipur / Nagaland still below 400). Per-capita is on geographical-area population (resident), not consumption-weighted — large industrial-export states (e.g. Chhattisgarh, Sikkim) post inflated numbers because the power they generate is consumed elsewhere.
indicators.methodology_vintage: RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 edition, Table 138. Originating data: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power.

indicators.label_long: State coal consumption (Mt, by fiscal year)
indicators.description_short: Per-state domestic coal consumption in million tonnes per fiscal year, summed across all coal grades (raw + washed + middlings + lignite). High values typically indicate hosting large thermal generation fleets (Maharashtra, UP, MP, Chhattisgarh) or heavy industry (steel, cement).
indicators.description_long: Where coal is burned, not where it is mined. Companion to state-installed-capacity-allocated-mw (coal facet) and state-electricity-generation-gwh (coal facet): a state with high coal consumption but low coal generation is using coal for industrial heat rather than power. The ``TOTAL COAL`` ICED rows are dropped to avoid double-counting; the lift sums the 4 grade-level rows (raw + washed + middlings + lignite) directly.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/energy/fuel-sources/coal/consumption-domestic-state`` (Coal Controller's Office / Ministry of Coal upstream). Aggregated by SUM of the 4 component grades (raw, washed, middlings, lignite); the precomputed ``TOTAL COAL`` rows are dropped to avoid double-counting.

indicators.description_short: Cumulative installed rooftop solar PV capacity in megawatts. Building-mounted (residential + commercial + industrial + public) only; utility-scale solar is separate and lives under state-installed-capacity-snapshot-mw-renewable.
indicators.description_long: Per the National Rooftop Solar Programme (MNRE), rooftop solar is owned by the building owner (household, factory, school), not by a power utility. A state's total solar fleet = rooftop + utility-scale. Gujarat dominates rooftop deployment by absolute MW (a decade of state-level scheme co-funding plus the SURYA Gujarat residential push). Rajasthan and Karnataka lead utility-scale solar but lag on rooftop because rooftop economics depend on retail tariff structure (which favours states with high commercial tariffs like Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu) more than insolation. Pair with state-installed-capacity-snapshot-mw-renewable to see whether a state's renewable footprint is utility-investor-led or owner-led.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NITI Aayog ICED ``/energy/renewable/solar/rooftop/state``. Originating data: MNRE / state nodal agencies via the National Rooftop Solar Programme. ICED is the federal aggregator; not the issuing authority.

indicators.description_short: Count of animals issued a 12-digit Pashu Aadhaar tag in each district. Tagged count, NOT actual population.
indicators.description_long: Pashu Aadhaar is the UIDAI-style 12-digit unique identifier issued by the National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM, Bharat Pashudhan) to individual animals. The count here is the number of TAGS issued in each district, NOT an estimate of the actual livestock population - coverage varies by state as the rollout is in progress. Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the 10 atomic-species children (cattle + buffalo + yak + mithun + sheep + goat + pig + horse + donkey + mule). No observation rows exist on disk for this id (per Hans D33.8 convention); the frontend sums the children at read time. The catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative, not a ranking.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan; vintages CY 2024 + FY 2024-25

Same Hans honest-renderer caveat applies: tagged count is NOT an estimate of the actual cattle population of the district; coverage varies by state. Vintages CY 2024 + FY 2024-25 both lifted from NDLM Bharat Pashudhan getAnimalRegistrationDistrictWise endpoint snapshot 2026-05-25.

indicators.description_short: Count of livestock owners completed Bharat Pashudhan registration in each district. Registered count, NOT all owning households.
indicators.description_long: Owner Registration is the Bharat Pashudhan workflow that records a livestock-owner profile (name + landholding bracket + gender) before any Pashu Aadhaar tag can be issued to that owner's animals. The count here is the number of REGISTERED owners in each district per the National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM), NOT an estimate of the total livestock-owning households - coverage varies by state as the rollout is in progress. Compute-on-read parent: the value is the sum of the 6 atomic land-holding bracket children (landless_marginal + small + semi_medium + medium + large + not_specified). No observation rows exist on disk for this id (per Hans D33.8 convention); the frontend sums the children at read time. The publisher also disaggregates by gender (male/female); this slice collapses the gender axis via SUM at write time and lifts on landholding only (gender retained in the meadow for a follow-up PR). The catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative, not a ranking.

indicators.label_long: NAIP IV artificial-insemination events per district
indicators.description_short: Count of artificial-insemination EVENTS performed in each district under NAIP IV. Repeat inseminations on the same animal are counted multiple times.
indicators.description_long: NAIP IV (National Artificial Insemination Programme, phase IV) is a select-district programme administered by the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD). Each row counts artificial-insemination EVENTS performed in the district during FY 2024-25 - NOT unique animals inseminated. Repeat inseminations on the same dam are counted multiple times (an animal may need 2-3 cycles before conception). 8 states/UTs (Kerala, Punjab, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Delhi, Lakshadweep, A&N, D&NH+D&D) report zero coverage upstream and are GENUINELY ABSENT from this fact-table - that is correct, not a defect: NAIP IV is select-district, and a missing state means out-of-scope, not zero-result. Catalogue carries comparability=directional_only and renderer_rules=[no_rank_table] - the renderer suppresses rank-table views and labels the choropleth illustrative.
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan NAIP IV district endpoint; vintage FY 2024-25 snapshot 2026-05-25

indicators.description_short: State total of pregnancy-diagnosis EVENTS performed under NAIP IV, summed from districts. A single dam may be diagnosed multiple times.
indicators.description_long: State-grain aggregate of district-livestock-naip-iv-pregnancy-diagnoses. Sum of district event-counts; materialised at canonical-write time per ADR-0043. Same select-district honesty applies: 8 states report zero coverage upstream and are absent from this fact-table (not zero). Catalogue carries comparability=directional_only + renderer_rules=[no_rank_table].
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan NAIP IV; FY 2024-25 (state aggregate of district events)

indicators.description_short: State total of calves born from NAIP IV inseminations, summed from districts. Sex split collapsed via SUM at district lift.
indicators.description_long: State-grain aggregate of district-livestock-naip-iv-calves-born. Sum of district calf-counts; materialised at canonical-write time per ADR-0043 (a second SUM atop the already sex-collapsed district rows; both derivations are honest). Same select-district honesty applies: 8 states report zero NAIP IV coverage upstream and are genuinely absent. Catalogue carries comparability=directional_only + renderer_rules=[no_rank_table].
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan NAIP IV; FY 2024-25 (state aggregate; sex collapsed via SUM at district)

indicators.description_short: State total of unique farmers reached by NAIP IV inseminations, summed from districts.
indicators.description_long: State-grain aggregate of district-livestock-naip-iv-farmers-benefitted. Sum of district farmer-counts; materialised at canonical-write time per ADR-0043. Note: this sum may double-count farmers operating across multiple districts in the same state (the underlying meadow rows are district-scoped without a cross-district farmer-uid). Hans honest-renderer: treat as upper bound on unique farmers in the state. 8 zero-coverage states genuinely absent. Catalogue carries comparability=directional_only + renderer_rules=[no_rank_table].
indicators.methodology_vintage: NDLM Bharat Pashudhan NAIP IV; FY 2024-25 (state aggregate; may double-count farmers across districts)
